method: A systematic sample of 64 of the census's 840 repeat legs: every 13th by launch time from the 7th (scripts/survey-repeats-sample.mjs). Each was read from a digest (scripts/survey-repeats-digests.mjs) by two readers, A and B, each an in-session subagent of the frontier tier split across two sessions of 32 digests, against the rubric below, fixed before any digest was read. Neither saw the other's codes; B read in reverse order. Disagreements were adjudicated by the author from the digest, with both codes in view; the reason is recorded.
rubric:
# Repeat-leg coding rubric (LIN-3174) — fixed before any digest was read

Each digest is about ONE repeat leg: a plan, plan-review, review (implementation review) or close-out session
that ran on a ticket where an earlier session of the same kind had already run. The digest gives the ticket's
leg timeline (every fresh session: its kind and launch time; the repeat being coded is marked `<<< THE REPEAT
BEING CODED`, the previous leg of its kind `<<< the previous leg of this kind`), every ticket comment in time
order (inside the window that matters, whole up to 3,000 characters; outside it, the first 300), every commit
naming the ticket in either repo with lines changed by class (`prod`, `test`, `docs`, `other`), and the
repeat's own launch prompt when it could be fetched. Comment headings are labelled by a heuristic ("heading
reads as") and a verdict reader; both can be wrong, so read the text.

Read only what is in the digest. Do not look anything up elsewhere.

## 1. `reason`: why did this repeat run? Pick the ONE code that best explains why a second (or later) session of
this kind was launched, judged from what happened between the previous leg of this kind and this one.

- `changes-requested` — a verdict asked for changes and this leg is the next round of the loop: a plan-review
  sent the plan back, so a new plan leg ran, or the revised plan is being re-reviewed; a code review sent the
  change back, so a new review ran on the fixes; a close-out held, and a new close-out ran after the hold was
  addressed.
- `plan-revised-after-research` — the plan (or its review) was re-run because research, a spike, a human
  answer or new information changed what the plan should be, not because a gate asked for changes.
- `staleness-regrounding` — the earlier leg's output had gone stale: main moved, the grounding commit drifted,
  a sibling landed, or enough time passed that the work had to be re-grounded.
- `failed-or-cut-off` — the previous session of this kind failed, crashed, was aborted, hit a limit, timed out
  or ended without posting its output, so it was run again.
- `rescue` — a supervisor or a person stepped in to unstick a ticket that had stalled or gone wrong, and this
  leg is part of that rescue (a re-plan or re-review ordered to recover the ticket).
- `duplicate-or-mistaken` — two launches overlapped, or a leg was launched again although the previous one
  had completed and nothing asked for another (a mistaken or duplicate dispatch).
- `scope-added` — scope was added to the ticket mid-way (a new requirement, a merged-in ticket, a widened
  acceptance), so planning or review had to run again over the new scope.
- `ci-red` — a CI failure after the earlier leg sent the ticket back through this kind of leg.
- `other` — none of these; say what in `note`.
- `unclear` — the digest does not show why.

If two apply, put the one that most directly caused the launch in `reason` and the other in `reason2`.

## 2. `bought`: what did THIS leg's round change?

Judge what followed this leg's output (its comment, verdict or plan) before the next leg of the same kind, or
before the ticket went Done.

- `substance` — it changed the plan's substance (a different approach, a new or removed step, a new case
  handled, a wrong claim corrected) or it led to a change in production code (a `prod` line change after the
  leg, made for something the leg raised or planned anew).
- `wording-tests` — it changed only wording, docs, the plan's presentation, or tests (no production line and
  no change of plan substance).
- `nothing` — it approved, confirmed or restated; nothing changed because of it.
- `unclear` — the digest cannot show it.

For a plan leg that is a repeat, `bought` asks whether the new plan differs in substance from the previous
one. For a plan-review, review or close-out repeat, it asks whether this round's findings or holds changed
the plan's substance or production code.

## 3. For plan-review and review repeats only (otherwise `na`):

- `newFinding` — `yes` if this round raised at least one finding that no earlier round of the same kind on this
  ticket raised; `no` if it only re-checked earlier findings or approved; `unclear`.
- `real` — for a new finding: `yes` if it was a genuine defect or gap (acted on, and the digest shows it was
  wrong before), `no` if it was rejected, a false alarm, or only a nit; `unclear`; `na` when `newFinding` is
  not `yes`.

## 4. `note` and `evidence`

`evidence`: the timestamp(s) of the comment(s) or commit(s) you relied on. `note`: one sentence, at most 30
words, saying what happened. Do not quote more than a sentence.

## Output

Return a JSON array, one object per digest, in digest order:
`{"digest": "07", "reason": "...", "reason2": null, "bought": "...", "newFinding": "yes|no|unclear|na", "real": "yes|no|unclear|na", "evidence": "...", "note": "..."}`
